bull.b: Improving revenue, gross margin, and operating results indicate better underlying operating leverage rather than reliance solely on reported growth. Q2’s revenue and EBITDA improvement reinforces the possibility that higher volumes, pricing, and cost control can support stronger earnings over the next several quarters.

The expanding dairy RNG network provides a scalable platform for renewable fuel production and environmental-credit generation. Approved low-carbon pathways increase credit intensity per unit, while contracted dairies and additional digesters create a multi-period pipeline for volume and revenue growth.

MVR could structurally improve the Keyes plant’s economics by lowering energy consumption and carbon intensity simultaneously. Those savings may support recurring cash generation and improve eligibility for environmental credits, while the project’s grants and tax credits reduce part of the investment burden.

bear.b: Negative equity and rising debt materially restrict financial flexibility and increase dependence on refinancing or asset-level cash events. High leverage can absorb future operating improvements through interest and principal obligations, leaving less capacity to fund projects or withstand execution setbacks.

Continued negative operating and free cash flow shows that improved revenue and gross margin have not yet translated into self-funded operations. Ongoing losses and cash consumption increase external funding needs, constrain investment capacity, and make debt service more difficult during project ramp-up.

A meaningful portion of projected economics depends on government calculations and pathway approvals that remain uncertain in timing and scope. Delays or less favorable credit treatment could reduce expected revenue and cash flow, weakening the business case for planned expansion despite operational progress.
